tagline: An old town on the Tha Chin River — home of luk thung music, century-old markets, and a city where everything worth seeing sits close together
introHtml:
Suphan Buri sits in the lower central plains, under two hours' drive from Bangkok. Most people picture it as a city with its sights ready to go: Bueng Chawak, which has both a zoo and an aquarium; the Banharn-Jaemsai Tower in the middle of town; and the old riverside Sam Chuk Market on the Tha Chin, still very much alive. The province has deep history too, from the elephant-back battle site at Don Chedi to the ancient town of U Thong.

The other side of Suphan Buri is luk thung country, the birthplace of several famous singers, with a memorial and museum that tell that story specifically. Outside town you'll find wide rice fields broken up by old temples and a buffalo village. If you'd rather travel without much planning, come to Suphan Buri and tick off the spots one by one — it works well for a family trip or a self-drive weekend.
bestTime: November–February, when the weather is cool and pleasant — good for walking Sam Chuk Market, visiting Bueng Chawak, and temple-hopping all day without the heat

highlights.name: Bueng Chawak
highlights.blurb: A large freshwater lake with both a freshwater and saltwater aquarium, a zoo, and a big aviary. It's the family spot most people think of first when they think of Suphan Buri.

highlights.name: Sam Chuk Century-Old Market
highlights.blurb: An old market on the Tha Chin River where people still live and trade for real — wooden shophouses, local food, and the Khun Chamnong House Museum for a look at old town life.

highlights.name: Banharn-Jaemsai Tower
highlights.blurb: A tower in the middle of Chaloem Phatra Rachini Park in town. Go up for a 360-degree view over Suphan Buri — a landmark right in the city centre.

highlights.name: Don Chedi Monument
highlights.blurb: The memorial to King Naresuan's elephant-back duel, paired with a large chedi. It's a key historical site tied to the province.

highlights.name: Mangkon Sawan Dragon Shrine
highlights.blurb: A shrine and Dragon Descendants Museum that tells the story of the Chinese community and its history through a large dragon tunnel in the centre of town.

highlights.name: Luk Thung Heartland
highlights.blurb: Suphan Buri is the birthplace of several luk thung singers, with a memorial and stories of the genre to follow. It's a character people closely associate with the province.

foodScene.name: Fish Noodle Soup (kuaytiao pla)
foodScene.note: A Suphan Buri specialty — a smooth, balanced broth with sliced fish. Several long-running shops in town and along the roadsides.

foodScene.name: Boat Noodles (kuaytiao ruea)
foodScene.note: The province is in the central plains' boat-noodle belt — small bowls with a dark, rich broth that you order several at a time at riverside and roadside shops.

foodScene.name: Tha Chin River Fish
foodScene.note: Fresh freshwater fish from the Tha Chin River — grilled, in tom yam, or as chu chi — at the riverside restaurants around the province.

foodScene.name: Sali Suphan and Local Sweets
foodScene.note: Soft sali sponge cake is a long-standing Suphan Buri gift to take home, sold at shops in town and at Sam Chuk Market.

foodScene.name: Sam Chuk Market Eats
foodScene.note: The old riverside market has plenty of local food to graze on — noodles, Thai sweets, old-style coffee, and fried snacks from the stalls.

foodScene.name: Isan Food
foodScene.note: Som tam, grilled chicken, and laap are easy to find around town and along the roads — bold flavours that suit a road trip.

foodScene.name: Mu Krata (Thai BBQ Hotpot)
foodScene.note: A popular dinner for locals, with several shops to choose from — relaxed atmosphere and friendly prices.

foodScene.name: Cafés in Town and by the Rice Fields
foodScene.note: Small cafés both in the city and out by the rice fields make good stops for a coffee between sights.

attractions.name: Bueng Chawak
attractions.blurb: A big freshwater lake with an aquarium, a zoo, and an aviary — half a day to a full day's worth. It's the province's main family attraction.

attractions.name: Sam Chuk Century-Old Market
attractions.blurb: A living old market on the Tha Chin River — wooden shophouses, local food, and the Khun Chamnong House Museum to walk through.

attractions.name: Banharn-Jaemsai Tower
attractions.blurb: A tower in a city park you can climb for views over town in every direction, surrounded by gardens for a stroll and a rest.

attractions.name: Don Chedi Monument
attractions.blurb: The memorial to King Naresuan and a large chedi — the historic site of the elephant-back battle, tied to the province.

attractions.name: Mangkon Sawan Dragon Shrine
attractions.blurb: A shrine and Dragon Descendants Museum where you walk through a dragon tunnel to learn Chinese history in the centre of town.

attractions.name: U Thong Ancient Town
attractions.blurb: A Dvaravati-era ancient town with the U Thong National Museum and ruins scattered around — good for anyone who likes history.

attractions.name: Thai Buffalo Conservation Village
attractions.blurb: A village that recreates farming life and raises Thai buffalo, with a buffalo show and traditional Thai houses for kids to see up close.

attractions.name: Rice Fields and the Tha Chin Riverside
attractions.blurb: Outside town it's wide rice fields broken up by old temples and riverside parks — easy to drive or cycle along to see local life.
